title: Musakhan (Sumac Chicken with Onions on Flatbread)
summary: Chicken is marinated in sumac and warm spices, roasted until deep golden, then piled onto crisped flatbreads with soft sumac onions, toasted pine nuts and parsley.

ingredients.item: bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
fine sea salt or table salt
large flatbreads (taboon, markook or thick pitta), about 80 g each

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Mix half the oil with 2 tablespoons of the sumac, the allspice, cumin, cinnamon, garlic, lemon juice, ¾ teaspoon of salt and the pepper, then rub it all over the chicken. Marinate in the fridge for 1-3 hours, or overnight if you have the time, so the spices properly flavour the meat rather than just sitting on the surface. About 20 minutes before roasting, heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan).

steps.title: Roast the chicken
steps.text: Roast the chicken skin-up in the tin for 40-45 minutes, until deep golden and the thigh meat reaches 80°C.

steps.title: Soften the onions
steps.text: While the chicken roasts, cook the sliced onions in the remaining oil with ¼ teaspoon of salt over medium heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring now and then, until completely soft and pale golden. Don't let them caramelise or go dark: they should stay sweet and silky. Stir in the remaining sumac once they're done, so its flavour stays bright.

steps.title: Toast the pine nuts
steps.text: In a dry pan, toast the pine nuts over medium-low heat for 3-4 minutes, shaking the pan often, until golden. Keep a close eye on them, as pine nuts burn very quickly once they start to colour.

steps.title: Crisp the flatbreads
steps.text: With the oven raised to 220°C (200°C fan), brush the flatbreads with the roasting juices or onion oil, spread over the sumac onions, and bake on trays for 5-7 minutes until the edges turn crisp.

steps.title: Assemble and serve
steps.text: Top each flatbread with chicken, either left whole or pulled from the bone, and spoon over any remaining roasting juices. Finish with the toasted pine nuts, parsley and an extra scattering of sumac.

tips: Cook the onions until soft and pale golden, not caramelised. Dark, caramelised onions turn the dish sweet and heavy and hide the sharp, lemony sumac.
Watch the pine nuts closely once they go in the pan, as they can burn within seconds of turning golden.
Check the chicken thigh reaches 80°C before taking it out, since bone-in pieces can look done on the outside before they're fully cooked through.
Brush the flatbreads with the flavourful roasting juices rather than plain oil for the best flavour.
Add the sumac to the onions after cooking, not during, so its tangy flavour stays fresh rather than fading in the pan.
storage: Keep the chicken and onions in the fridge separately from the bread for up to 3 days. Reheat the chicken and onions until piping hot (74°C) and crisp the bread briefly in the oven before assembling again, rather than freezing the assembled dish. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
